method: A puzzle starts from a Latin square: the cyclic square has its rows, columns and symbols shuffled, and the four visibility counts (seen from the top, bottom, left and right of every line) are computed. Clues are then removed one at a time in random order; a removal is kept only when an exhaustive search still finds exactly one solution, and puzzles that cannot reach the difficulty target are discarded and rebuilt. The search enforces each row and column as an all-different set, chooses the empty cell with the fewest legal heights, and prunes a line when its visible-tower count can no longer reach the clue: the count of records in the filled prefix is a lower bound and that count plus the unfilled positions is an upper bound. Difficulty is the number of clues left: 4×4 keeps 12, 9 or 7 of 16; 5×5 keeps 16, 12 or 9 of 20; 6×6 keeps 20, 15 or 11-13 of 24. A 6×6 build takes about a second in a browser, so the page serves 6×6 puzzles from a fixed set of 24 that were generated and uniqueness-checked the same way, eight per difficulty. Answers are checked against the single stored solution, and repeated heights in a row or column are flagged as you type. Everything runs in this page: no network requests, accounts, uploads or stored data.
